correctness.rationale: For selected squares D the line-graph support H_D is bipartite on occupied rows and columns. Dominating every board square iff all rows or all columns occupied; induced graph connected iff the occupied-edge support is connected. If both sides full, deleting a cycle edge or a leaf edge preserves connected domination; inclusion-minimality forces exactly one side full. With only rows full the supporting graph must be a tree and every occupied column nonleaf; otherwise removing an edge preserves connectivity/domination. Conversely removing any edge either disconnects selected edges or isolates a full-side row, violating domination because another column is empty. Symmetry handles other family. Bipartite Prüfer words of lengths c-1 and p-1 have p^{c-1} possibilities and c!S(p-1,c) surjective column words, with binom(q,c) choices of columns; the dual summand similarly follows. The ranges yield [p,2p-2] U [q,q+p-2], including p=q=2. Independent original-graph subset enumeration and direct Stirling coefficient computation agreed on seven boards through 4x4; the tree bijection, not finite enumeration, proves generality.

originality.rationale: Mertens 2024 evaluates the ordinary domination polynomial of rook graphs by row/column coverage, but counts dominating sets including disconnected and nonminimal configurations; its evaluated theorem does not give the one-sided-leaf-tree iff classification or Stirling minimal-connected polynomial. Abu-Khzam et al ESA 2022 give general minimal connected dominating set enumeration algorithms and lower bounds rather than this exact labeled rook-graph polynomial. Classical Prüfer counting is acknowledged; the new contribution is the exact structural two-family identification and gap spectrum. Full primary PDFs were accessible and examined in relevant mathematical sections. Unindexed equivalent rook-graph minimal connected dominating polynomial remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The distinction between minimum-size and inclusion-minimal connected domination is natural and mathematically significant. The exact polynomial enumerates all irredundant connected covering configurations via a nontrivial bipartite tree class; the complete achievable-cardinality spectrum has arbitrarily long holes already for two-row boards. This gap behavior is not implied by ordinary domination coefficients or general enumeration algorithms and can benchmark structural domination problems.

limitations: Only inclusion-minimal connected dominating sets, not arbitrary dominating-set polynomial or unrelated domination variants.
